Who is credited with discovering Ceres?
Ceres (dwarf planet): Giuseppe Piazzi. Ceres is a dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
This localized collection of pus builds up within body tissue, usually from bacterial infection, causing redness, pain, warmth, and swelling. What is it?
Abscess is a collection of pus that has built up within the tissue of the body, usually caused by bacterial infection.
First described by Othniel C. Marsh in 1877, this late Jurassic theropod's name means 'different lizard,' a nod to its unusually lightweight vertebrae — what dinosaur is it?
Allosaurus is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived 155 to 143 million years ago during the late Jurassic period (latest Oxfordian to latest Tithonian ages).

Named in 1835 from the Greek for 'flower' and 'dark blue,' these pH-shifting pigments paint blueberries, black rice, and some autumn leaves anything from red to purple to nearly black — what are they?

Anthocyanin (from Ancient Greek (nthos) 'flower' and / (kuneos/kuanos) 'dark blue'), also called anthocyans, are water-soluble vacuolar pigments that, depending on their pH, may appear red, pink, purple, blue, or black.
First described in 1740, this flowering-plant family rivals only the orchid family in sheer number of species, with over 32,000 recognized today — what family is it?
Asteraceae is a large family of flowering plants that consists of over 32,000 known species in over 1,900 genera within the order Asterales.

This fluid-dynamics rule holds that a fluid's pressure drops as its speed increases; the Swiss physicist credited with it published the idea in 1738, though Leonhard Euler derived the actual equation — what's it called?
Bernoulli's principle is a key concept in fluid dynamics that relates pressure, speed and height.
This incurable, always-fatal disease of cattle causes abnormal behavior and trouble walking, with symptoms that may take four to five years to appear after infection — what is this disorder called?
Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), commonly known as mad cow disease, is an incurable and always fatal neurodegenerative disease of cattle.

One species in this genus of flowering shrubs, native to southern China and Indochina, has its leaves processed into the world's tea, while thousands of ornamental cultivars exist for the garden. Name the genus?
Camellia is a genus of flowering plants in the family Theaceae.
Taken by mouth with effects lasting about a day, this second-generation antihistamine treats hay fever, hives, and dermatitis with less drowsiness than older allergy medications — what is it?
Cetirizine is a second-generation peripherally selective antihistamine used to treat allergic rhinitis (hay fever), dermatitis, urticaria (hives), and runny nose.
Its Latin genus name literally means three-leaf, and this herbaceous legume, native to Europe, now grows worldwide in around 300 species — what plant is it?
Clover are plants of the genus Trifolium (from Latin tres 'three' and folium 'leaf').

This cosmopolitan bird family includes crows, ravens, magpies, and jays, and its roughly 135 species are known for remarkable intelligence, including self-awareness demonstrated in mirror tests — what's the family?
Corvidae is a cosmopolitan family of oscine passerine birds that contains the crows, ravens, rooks, magpies, jackdaws, jays, treepies, choughs, and nutcrackers.

First patented in Germany in 1920, then independently synthesized by an American chemist in 1932 and marketed in German-speaking Europe as Permonid for its fast onset and short duration, what is this semi-synthetic opioid?
Desomorphine (or in some formulations known as Krokodil) is a semi-synthetic opioid commercialized by Roche, with powerful, fast-acting effects, such as sedation and analgesia.
Along with the platypus, this quill-covered Australian and New Guinean mammal is one of only two living egg-laying mammal groups, and its young are adorably called puggles — what is it?
Echidna are quill-covered monotremes (egg-laying mammals) belonging to the family Tachyglossidae, living in Australia and New Guinea.
This taxonomic family groups hedgehogs of Eurasia and Africa together with the furrier moonrats of Southeast Asia, and takes its name from the Latin for 'hedgehog' — what family is it?
Erinaceidae (from Latin erinaceus, "hedgehog") is a family in the order Eulipotyphla, consisting of the hedgehogs and moonrats.
This field of study, related to economics and business administration, is typically divided into personal, corporate, and public branches. What field is it?
Finance refers to monetary resources as well as the discipline that studies such resources, with related concepts such as money, currency, assets and liabilities.
Testimony at Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán's 2018 trial revealed suitcases stuffed with $3 million in bribes paid to this former Mexican security chief — who is he?
Genaro García Luna (born 10 July 1968) is a Mexican former government official and convicted drug trafficker.
This Italian-American motorsport boss ran a Formula One team for seven years before becoming CEO and owner of a MotoGP outfit — who is he?
Guenther Steiner (born 7 April 1965) is an Italian and American motorsport engineer and former team manager.
This seasonal state of low body temperature, slow breathing, and reduced metabolism helps some animals pass through winter months — what is it?
Hibernation is a state of minimal activity and metabolic reduction entered by some animal species.
First appearing in the fossil record in Egypt some 37 million years ago, this order of small African herbivores once rivaled odd-toed ungulates in size and diversity — which order?
Hyracoidea is a taxonomic order of mammals.

This English independent scientist invented the electron capture detector, was first to spot CFCs spread through the atmosphere, and proposed that the Earth behaves as one self-regulating system. Who was he?
James Lovelock (26 July 1919 - 26 July 2022) was an English independent scientist, environmentalist and futurist.
This Soviet-designed naval helicopter has spawned variants for assault transport, export, and civilian use, and still flies today from Russia to India -- which aircraft?

Kamov Ka-27 (NATO reporting name 'Helix') is a military helicopter developed for the Soviet Navy, and as of 2024 is in service in various countries including Russia, Ukraine, Vietnam, China, South Korea, and India.

A hybrid of the citron and the bitter orange believed to have originated in northeastern India around the 1st millennium BC, this small evergreen citrus tree bears a tart yellow fruit used worldwide — name the fruit?
Lemon (Citrus limon) is a species of small evergreen tree in the Citrus genus of the flowering plant family Rutaceae.
Dubbed the 'Queen of QVC' for her long-running shopping show and holding over 120 patents, this American entrepreneur is also an investor on the reality series Shark Tank — who is she?
Lori Greiner is an American television personality and entrepreneur.

This Milanese thinker was the first woman to write a mathematics handbook and the first appointed a mathematics professor — though she spent her final decades on theology and serving the poor. Who was she?
Maria Gaetana Agnesi (16 May 1718 - 9 January 1799) was a Milanese mathematician, philosopher, theologian, and humanitarian.

Named from Greek words meaning 'small head,' this congenital condition involves a smaller-than-normal head and can affect brain development, intellectual ability, and motor function — which disorder is it?
Microcephaly (from Neo-Latin microcephalia, from Ancient Greek mikrs "small" and kephal "head") is a medical condition involving a smaller-than-normal head.
Named for the strong odor males emit during rut to attract mates, this thick-coated Arctic hoofed mammal is called 'the bearded one' in Inuktitut — what's the species?
Muskox (Ovibos moschatus) is a hoofed mammal of the family Bovidae.
First isolated by Scottish physician Daniel Rutherford, which group-15 nonmetal with atomic number 7 is the most abundant species in Earth's atmosphere?
Nitrogen is a chemical element; it has symbol N and atomic number 7.
The heaviest living bird, this flightless African species can sprint at 70 km/h and lays the largest eggs of any land animal on Earth — what bird is it?

A Chinese singer famous for annual appearances on a widely watched Lunar New Year television gala, she has served as her country's First Lady since 2012 as the wife of its paramount leader — who is she?

Peng Liyuan (pinyin: Png Lyun; born 20 November 1962) is a Chinese singer who has served as the First Lady of China since 2012, as the wife of Xi Jinping, the General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party and paramount leader of China.
The sole genus in its plant subfamily, this evergreen conifer bears needle-like leaves in bunches of two to five and carries its seeds on woody cones — name the tree?
Pine is any conifer in the genus Pinus of the family Pinaceae.

This oral glucocorticoid medication suppresses the immune system and reduces inflammation in conditions like asthma and COPD, though long-term use risks side effects such as cataracts and bone loss — what's the drug called?
Prednisone is a glucocorticoid medication mostly used to suppress the immune system and decrease inflammation in conditions such as asthma, COPD, and rheumatologic diseases.
Element 88 on the periodic table, this silvery-white alkaline earth metal turns black when exposed to air and glows via radioluminescence as it radioactively decays — which element?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.

Usually hidden below the soil surface but sometimes growing aerial or aerating instead, these plant organs anchor a plant while drawing in the water and nutrients it needs to grow taller and faster — name them?
Root are the organs of a plant that are modified to provide anchorage for the plant and take in water and nutrients into the plant body, which allows plants to grow taller and faster.

Native to the North Pacific coasts, this marine mammal is the heaviest member of the weasel family yet one of the smallest marine mammals, insulated by the densest fur coat in the animal kingdom — what is it?
Sea otter (Enhydra lutris) is a marine mammal native to the coasts of the northern and eastern North Pacific Ocean.
Commonly but inaccurately nicknamed for a big cat it wasn't closely related to, this extinct genus of saber-toothed predator roamed the Americas until as recently as 8,200 years ago — which genus?
Smilodon is a genus of extinct felids. It is one of the best-known saber-toothed predators and prehistoric mammals.

Starting with fever and flu-like symptoms before the skin blisters and peels into painful raw patches, this severe drug-triggered skin reaction sits on the same disease spectrum as toxic epidermal necrolysis, only less severe — which condition?
Stevens–Johnson syndrome (SJS) is a type of severe skin reaction.

Tucked beneath the lateral fissure of the brain and named for its position near the head's temples, this region handles language comprehension, memory, and emotion — which part of the cerebral cortex?
Temporal lobe is one of the four major lobes of the cerebral cortex in the brain of mammals.
These brightly colored Neotropical birds are known for their oversized, vividly patterned bills, and their chicks hatch completely naked with no down feathers at all — what bird is it?
Toucan are Neotropical birds in the family Ramphastidae.
This member of the herpesvirus family causes chickenpox in children and, upon reactivation later in life, shingles in adults — what is it called?
Varicella zoster virus (VZV), also known as human herpesvirus 3 (HHV-3, HHV3), is one of nine known herpes viruses that can infect humans.
This broad category of limbless, tube-bodied animals ranges from microscopic creatures to a marine species measured at nearly 58 meters long — the longest animal on Earth — what are they called?
Worm are many different distantly related bilateral animals that typically have a long cylindrical tube-like body, no limbs, and usually no eyes.
This mucolytic drug is the go-to antidote for acetaminophen overdose, working by boosting glutathione to neutralize the drug's toxic byproducts — what is it?
Acetylcysteine: Medication used to treat overdose of paracetamol.
Twice President of the Swiss Confederation, this Social Democratic politician left the Federal Council in 2023 to become Secretary General of the Council of Europe — who is he?
Alain Berset: Swiss Federal Councillor from 2012 to 2023.
Nicknamed the boto for its rosy pink hue (especially in males), this South American toothed whale is the largest species of its kind found in a freshwater habitat — what is it?
Amazon river dolphin: Species of toothed whale. The position of the Araguaian river dolphin (I. araguaiaensis) within the clade is still unclear.
This American anthropologist studied women's weaving and blacksmithing work in Indonesia and later designed microcredit programs to fight rural poverty — who was she?
This pigmented ring of skin around the nipple contains sebaceous glands as well as the openings of the milk ducts — what's it called?
Areola: Pigmented area on the breast around the nipple.
The famous AL 288-1 skeleton nicknamed 'Lucy,' unearthed in Ethiopia's Afar region, belongs to which extinct East African hominin species that lived roughly 3.9 to 2.9 million years ago?
Australopithecus afarensis: Extinct hominid from the Pliocene of East Africa.
Coming on over about 48 hours, this temporary facial paralysis droops one side of the face and can heighten sensitivity to sound — what condition is it?
Bell's palsy: Facial paralysis. Bell's palsy is a type of facial paralysis that results in a temporary inability to control the facial muscles on the affected side of the face.
This organ stores urine received from the kidneys via the ureters before it exits through the urethra, and gives us the medical term 'cystitis' when inflamed — what is it?
Bladder: Organ in vertebrates that collects and stores urine from the kidneys before disposal.
Named from Greek words for 'slow' and 'heart,' this condition means a resting heart rate under 60 beats per minute — sometimes normal in well-conditioned athletes — which condition?
Bradycardia: Heart rate below the normal range.
Common in cancer, heart failure, and other serious illnesses, this syndrome causes muscle wasting that better nutrition alone can't reverse — what is it?
In 1886 this German engineer patented what's considered the first practical automobile, and his Mannheim company later merged with Daimler — who is he?
Carl Benz: German designer and engineer (1844–1929)
Documented anatomically since the time of Hippocrates over 2,000 years ago, this roughly 4-centimeter-long fibromuscular organ connects the vagina to the uterine cavity. What structure is this?
Cervix: Lower part of the uterus in the female reproductive system.
This Dutch scientist discovered Saturn's largest moon and invented the pendulum clock, the most accurate timekeeper for nearly three centuries — who is he?
Christiaan Huygens: Dutch mathematician and physicist (1629–1695)
Thought extinct since the age of dinosaurs 66 million years ago, this lobe-finned fish was found alive off the west Indian Ocean, more closely related to lungfish than typical fish — what is it?
Also known as the Cornelian cherry, this dogwood-family shrub or small tree is native to western and southern Europe as well as southwestern Asia — what's its scientific name?
Cornus mas: Species of flowering plant in the family Cornaceae.
This closed sac in the body, distinct from an abscess of pus, forms a shell of abnormal cells and may contain air, fluid, or semi-solid material — what is it, medically?
Cyst: Closed sac growth on the body. A cyst is a closed sac in the body, having a distinct envelope and division compared with the nearby tissue.

Found in many cough and cold medicines, this morphinan-class compound was approved by the FDA in 2022 as part of a rapid-acting antidepressant combo, but can act as a dissociative hallucinogen at high doses. What substance is it?
Dextromethorphan: Cough suppressant and dissociative drug.
Sold over the counter as Unisom and combined with vitamin B6 to ease morning sickness, this first-generation antihistamine is one of the world's most widely used sleep aids — which drug?
Doxylamine: First-generation antihistamine used as a short-term sedative and hypnotic (sleep aid)
Appointed to the Supreme Court by Barack Obama in 2010, this former Harvard Law dean became the fourth woman ever to serve as a justice — who is she?
Elena Kagan: US Supreme Court justice since 2010.
A rod-shaped gut bacterium that's mostly harmless or even helpful — some strains produce vitamin K2 and fend off nastier microbes — what is its name?
Sold in Italian restaurants as branzino, this slow-growing ocean fish is the most important species farmed commercially in the Mediterranean — what fish is it?
European seabass: Species of fish. It is one of only six species in its family, Moronidae, collectively called the temperate basses.
This beetle family produces light mainly at twilight to attract mates — though some females mimic another species' flash pattern just to lure and eat the males — what are they commonly called?
Firefly: Family of beetles. The Lampyridae are a family of elateroid beetles with more than 2,400 described species, many of which are light-emitting.
Only chefs with three-plus years of rigorous training may legally prepare this potentially lethal Japanese pufferfish dish, whose poison is tetrodotoxin — what is it?
Recognized as the world's longest ray-finned fish, this ribbon-shaped, silvery-blue deep-sea creature is often blamed for sea-serpent legends — which fish?
Giant oarfish: Species of oceanic ray-finned fish.
Dating back roughly 250 million years to the early Triassic, this ground-dwelling insect hears through an organ on its abdomen and leaps away from danger using powerful hind legs — what is it?
Grasshopper: Common name for a group of insects.
This British mathematician has studied the math of dating and pandemics, delivered the Royal Institution's 2019 Christmas Lectures, and hosted BBC's 'Secret Genius of Modern Life' — who is she?
Hannah Fry: British mathematician and broadcaster (born 1984)
Found in trace amounts in modern gasoline blends, this colorless, six-carbon alkane boils at about 69°C and serves as a cheap, low-reactivity solvent — what is it?
A colorless gas that throws off white fumes the moment it meets moist air, it turns into a familiar strong acid once dissolved in water — which compound, formula HCl?
Hydrogen chloride: Chemical compound. Hydrogen chloride gas and hydrochloric acid are important in technology and industry.

Also known as the spectacled or binocellate snake, this reptile from South Asia is one of the 'Big Four' species responsible for most snakebites in the region and is revered in Hindu mythology — which snake?
Indian cobra: Species of snake. The species is native to the Indian subcontinent, and is a member of the "Big Four" species that are responsible for the most snakebite cases in Sri Lanka and India.
This English inventor and industrial designer created the bagless vacuum cleaner using cyclonic separation, and by 2023 was the UK's fifth-richest person — who is he?
James Dyson: British inventor and businessman (born 1947)

Born John Chapman, this American pioneer nurseryman planted seed-grown apple trees across Pennsylvania, Ohio and beyond, becoming a folk hero in his own lifetime for his kindness and conservation. By what nickname do we know him?
This Gram-negative rod bacterium can turn deadly if aspirated into the lungs, producing a telltale bloody, brownish-yellow jelly-like sputum — which pathogen?
Klebsiella pneumoniae: Species of bacterium. Klebsiella pneumoniae is a Gram-negative, non-motile, encapsulated, lactose-fermenting, facultative anaerobic, rod-shaped bacterium.
This Hungarian-born physicist conceived the nuclear chain reaction in 1933, then drafted the letter Einstein signed that launched the Manhattan Project — who was he?
Leo Szilard: Hungarian-American physicist and inventor (1898–1964)

A four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft, this American plane is a comprehensive update of an older transport design, with over 500 delivered to 26 operators worldwide as of 2022. What aircraft is this?
Lockheed Martin C-130J Super Hercules: Military transport aircraft. The C-130J is a comprehensive update of the Lockheed C-130 Hercules, with new engines, flight deck, and other systems.
A chemical engineer and physician who also served in the Peace Corps, she became the first African-American woman in space aboard Endeavour in 1992 — who is she?
Mae Jemison: American astronaut, doctor and engineer (born 1956)

Endemic to North America and known for long, upward-curving upper tusks with little to no lower tusks, this proboscidean's genus split from other elephant relatives at least 28 million years ago — which ancient beast?
This scientific field studies the atmosphere and short-term weather phenomena, with applications spanning aviation, agriculture, and disaster management — what field is it?
Meteorology: Scientific study of the atmosphere focusing on weather forecasting.
Sold as Remeron, this atypical tetracyclic antidepressant is often chosen when depression comes tangled with anxiety or insomnia — which drug is it?
Mirtazapine: Antidepressant medication. Mirtazapine, sold under the brand name Remeron among others, is an atypical tetracyclic antidepressant, and as such is used primarily to treat depression.
Serving as Turkey's minister overseeing environment and climate, who is set to preside over the 2026 UN Climate Change Conference, COP31?
A healthy kidney contains up to 1.5 million of these microscopic filtering units, each pairing a capillary tuft with a cup-shaped capsule — what is it called?
Nephron: Microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney.
The largest structure inside a eukaryotic cell's nucleus, this site of ribosome assembly also helps form signal recognition particles and responds to cellular stress — what is it?
Nucleolus: Largest structure in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells. The nucleolus also participates in the formation of signal recognition particles and plays a role in the cell's response to stress.

Believed to be the world's fourth-leading cause of disability, this degenerative joint disease comes from the breakdown of cartilage and bone, often striking the fingertips, thumb base, knees, and hips — what is it?
Osteoarthritis: Form of arthritis caused by degeneration of joints.

Also called the blue passionflower, this South American vine climbs via tendrils to 10 metres, bears fragrant blue-white blooms with a fringed coronal filament, and produces an edible but not particularly tasty orange fruit — which plant is it?
Passiflora caerulea: Species of flowering plant in the passion flower family.
Usually caused by a virus but sometimes by strep bacteria, this inflammation of the back of the throat brings on a sore throat, fever, and sometimes a hoarse voice — what is it called?
Pharyngitis: Inflammation of the back of the throat. Pharyngitis is a type of upper respiratory tract infection.
Used in randomized clinical trials as a genuine-looking but pharmacologically inert stand-in — like a sugar pill or saline shot — what's this sham treatment called?
Placebo: Substance or treatment of no therapeutic value.
This rare genetic disorder linked to chromosome 15 leaves affected children constantly hungry, often leading to obesity, alongside a narrow forehead and small hands and feet — what is it?
Prader–Willi syndrome: Genetic disorder involving an imprinted genomic region.
This term covers the laws, regulations, and government actions that address issues from education to healthcare to transportation — what is it?
Public policy: Government proposals, principles and actions.
Found in the Atlas Mountains as the only member of its family native to Africa, this large ruminant's males are called stags and females are hinds — what species is it?
Red deer: Species of hoofed mammal.

This interdisciplinary field combines a power source, mechanical construction, control circuits, and software to design machines that assist humans in fields from medicine to space exploration — what is it?
Robotics: Design, construction, use, and application of robots.
Native to Mexico and Guatemala, this mint-family plant is prized for its hydrophilic seeds known as chia — what's its scientific name?
Salvia hispanica: Species of flowering plant in the mint family.
Located between the bladder and the rectum in male mammals, this paired accessory gland produces most of the fluid released during ejaculation — what is it?
Seminal vesicles: Pair of simple tubular glands.
Living in damp spots like rotting wood, these polyphyletic organisms combine into fruiting bodies that release spores to help decompose dead plants — what are they?
A competitive physical activity that maintains or improves physical ability and skills, this can involve teams or individuals and may be open to broad participation or restricted. What is this?
Sport: Forms of competitive activity, usually physical.
Born from Russia's PAK FA programme begun in 1999 and carrying the internal name T-50, this twin-engine jet was the first Russian military aircraft built with stealth technology — what is it?
Sukhoi Su-57: Russian stealth multirole fighter aircraft.
Nicknamed the brown raptor, this nocturnal bird of prey nests in tree hollows across Europe and is so territorial that evicted youngsters may starve — what is it?
Tawny owl: Stocky medium-sized owl species.

Marked by platelet counts that fall too low — sometimes below 50,000 per microliter and requiring emergency care — this blood disorder is the most common coagulation problem in ICU patients — what is it called?
Thrombocytopenia: Abnormally low levels of platelets in the blood.
This spiral-shaped bacterium, spread mainly through sexual contact and known only to infect humans and baboons, causes syphilis along with yaws and bejel — what is it?
Treponema pallidum: Species of bacterium. T. pallidum can enter the host through mucosal membranes or open lesions in the skin and is primarily spread through sexual contact.
This medical specialty treats the kidneys, bladder and urinary tract, along with the male reproductive organs, covering conditions from infections to kidney stones — which field of medicine?
Urology: Medical specialty on the urinary and reproductive systems. The urinary and reproductive tracts are closely linked, and disorders of one often affect the other.
As DuPont's leader of organic chemistry, this American chemist laid the groundwork for neoprene and is credited with inventing one world-changing synthetic fiber — who was he?
Wallace Carothers: American chemist and inventor (1896–1937)
With atomic number 54, this dense, colorless noble gas was the first to form a stable chemical compound, and now doubles as a general anesthetic and ion-thruster propellant — which element?
Xenon: Chemical element with atomic number 54 (Xe). It is a dense, colorless, odorless noble gas found in Earth's atmosphere in trace amounts.
